$comment: The words an amount is written or said with, in Urdu script, Roman Urdu and English, for the amount grammar (docs/roadmap/amount-parser.md): mm_core's parseAmount and formatAmountWords, and later its findAmounts and the TypeScript ports. Written by hand and NOT YET REVIEWED by a native speaker (reviewed: false; the review is work item 2, through docs/roadmap/urdu-review.md; review.check_first lists what to look at first). In every list the first spelling is the one to write; the others are only read. A spelling, after normalise, belongs to one entry only: a number, a fraction, a multiplier, a currency marker, a paisa word, a foreign currency, a filler or a connector. A 'write' object names the spelling formatAmountWords writes for one and for any other count. ambiguous lists tokens with a second everyday meaning: 'free_text' tokens are read in a single amount field and make an amount in free text ambiguous; 'spaced' tokens are also read in free text when joined to digits ('50k', '5mn'); 'always' tokens are never read and make any amount they touch ambiguous, because ignoring them would misread it. A free_text token with read_after is read in free text too after one of those cues, where its other meaning cannot be meant: 'fraction', a fraction word just before it ('sawa do lakh'); 'marker', one of currency.markers just before it (a sign written before an amount: Rs, Rs., PKR, the rupee sign) and a multiplier somewhere after it ('Rs do hazar', but not 'rs do' or 'rupay do', 'give the money'). homographs lists other meanings the grammar's other rules already keep apart, for the review. A multiplier's plural forms are read only after a number ('5 lakhs'); on their own ('lakhs of rupees') they are vague and ambiguous. not_included lists spellings left out on purpose. Every addition needs a vector in contracts/amount_vectors.json.

check_first.why: sawa, sarhe, paune, derh, dhai: their values, min_number (sarhe from 3, paune from 2) and alone (sawa lakh 125,000, paune sau 75); whether aadha, pauna, paun and pao should be read rather than refused; the error in tl-ur-fractional.

the paisa words are read only at the end, after a rupee marker and a number from 1 to 99 ('pachas rupay bees paise'); anywhere else they also mean 'money' and are refused. Confirm the rule, and the written forms ek paisa, ایک پیسہ, ek rupaya, ایک روپیہ.

check_first.why: refused because they also mean 'all'; confirm, and say whether سارے in Urdu script needs the same.
6, 22, 23, 51, 53, 54, 63, 64, 67, 74, 75, 77, 78, 79, 81, 91, ھزار: the sources disagree; confirm each variant, and چوون and ستتر, left out.

every Roman spelling after the first is general knowledge; check the first one (it is what the read-back writes) for 6, 23, 51 to 58, 61 to 68, 71 to 79, 90 to 99, and the near pairs 23 teis and 30 tees, 24 chaubis and 26 chhabbis.

do and دو, سوا, اسی, بہتر, انیس, نواسی and nawasi (also 'granddaughter'), sattar, saath, sath, bara, tera, sat, so, arab, hajar, mn and bn spaced (Roman main or mein, and ban or bana): refused in free text; confirm the other meaning is common enough. 'do hazar rupay' at the start of a message is refused too, on purpose: parseAmount also reads spans cut out of a longer message, where 'bhej' may come before.
کھرب (kharab is refused), ملین and بلین in Urdu, hajar, karod, krore.
روپئے, روپوں, rupaya, rupiya; whether 'Re. 1' should be read.
refused: is 'do lakh aur pachas hazar' always 250,000?

check_first.what: do and دو after a fraction word or a currency marker
check_first.why: read in free text there (read_after), since 'give' cannot follow sawa, paune or Rs; after Rs, PKR or the rupee sign only when a multiplier follows ('Rs do hazar'), so 'rs do' and 'rupay do' ('give the money') are refused. Confirm no common phrase breaks this. سوا after Rs is read the same way.

'ek lakh bees', '5 lakh 50', '1 crore 20', 'das lakh pachas': people often leave out the next unit down (1,20,000; 5.5 lakh; 1.2 crore), so a lakh, million, crore, arab or kharab followed only by a number that would fit that unit is refused (elidedMultiplier). A rupee word straight after the number pins it as rupees ('ek lakh bees rupay' is 100,020), which is how the read-back writes it: confirm that people who drop the unit also drop the rupee word. Also say whether hazar needs the same rule: is 'do hazar paanch' 2,005 or 2,500?

اڑھائی, arhai, arhaai, adhai, adhaai (dhai); dhed, dhedh, ڈیڑ (derh); ساڑے (sarhe); the ou spellings chouda, choudah, choubees, choubis, chountees, chouwalees, chounsath, chouhattar, chourasi, chouranwe; pacchees, pacchis, dass, chey, chhey, pichattar; kror, caror, carore. Confirm each is a spelling people use. ik and panj are left out: say whether the pilot should add them.

normalise.$comment: Applied to the text, and to every spelling here, before matching. It extends the plan's normalisation (digits, direction marks, lower case) with the Arabic keyboard's letters, the full-width comma and full stop, the invisible characters that copying from chat apps and right-to-left text carries, and marks that never tell two number words apart. Each fold is one code point for one or two, so a span can be mapped back to the original text.
normalise.digits: As normalizeDigits (packages/mm_core/lib/src/text/digits.dart): Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic (Urdu) and full-width digits become ASCII.

fractions.note: One and a half, on its own or before a multiplier: ڈیڑھ لاکھ 150,000; derh sau 150. Takes no number after it. dedh is the roadmap's spelling.

Two and a half, on its own or before a multiplier: dhai lakh 250,000. Takes no number after it. اڑھائی (arhai, adhai) is the Punjab-influenced form, as common in Pakistan; both are read, and ڈھائی is written.

A quarter less than the number after it: paune do lakh 175,000. alone: before a multiplier with no number it takes one (paune sau 75). tl-ur-fractional gives 'paune aaTh' as 7 1/2, an error: a quarter less than eight is 7 3/4, as tl-hi-fractional gives.
A half more than the number after it: sarhe teen hazar 3,500. From three upwards; 1 1/2 and 2 1/2 are derh and dhai. Never alone. Roman sare, saray and saare (also 'all') are refused; see ambiguous.
A quarter more than the number after it: sawa do lakh 225,000. alone: before a multiplier with no number it takes one (sawa lakh 125,000; sawa sau 125). سوا is also 'except' after کے; see ambiguous.

multipliers.note: ھزار: tl-ur-cardinal. hajar is how hazar is written where z is said as j, and is also a name; k is read joined to digits ('50k'); see ambiguous.
lakh and lac: cldr-en, parseMoneyInput. CLDR's short form L is refused; see ambiguous.
Owner question 1, as recommended: million and mn everywhere; a bare m only in a single amount field; see ambiguous. ملین is the English word as Urdu newspapers write it (general knowledge).
cr: cldr-en, parseMoneyInput; refused in free text, where bank messages use Cr for 'credit'; see ambiguous.
Short-scale billion (10^9), as Pakistani English uses it. بلین is the Urdu word as Urdu newspapers write it (general knowledge). Roman arab is also 'Arab'; see ambiguous.
cldr-ur-rbnf and cldr-ur use کھرب for 10^11. Roman kharab is also 'bad' (خراب) and is refused; see ambiguous. English has no single word.

currency.note: Every marker parseMoneyInput reads is here (Rs, Rs., PKR, ₨, rupee, rupees, روپے, روپیہ, روپیے, a trailing /-); receipts also write /=. markers are the signs written before an amount, the cue read_after names. cldr-ur gives پاکستانی روپیہ and the symbol Rs; cldr-en gives PKR.

paisa.note: A hundredth of a rupee. Read only at the end of an amount, after a rupee marker and a number from 1 to 99 ('pachas rupay bees paise', 'ایک سو روپے پچاس پیسے'); anywhere else they also mean 'money' ('paise de do') and make the amount ambiguous, and '50 paise' alone is half a rupee, not 50 rupees. The oblique پیسوں stays in ambiguous.

foreign_currency.note: Owners abroad (decision 1) may write amounts in the currency they earn. An amount next to one of these is not in rupees and is never read as rupees. ₹ is the Indian rupee. sar (Saudi riyal) is also Roman 'head' (سر); a refusal there only asks the person to confirm.

fillers.note: 'only', as on cheques and receipts ('Rupees fifty thousand only', 'پچاس ہزار روپے صرف'). Never changes the amount.

connectors.note: British English joins the last number of a group with 'and' ('one hundred and fifty', 'one thousand and five'). Read only in a single amount field, and only before the last number of a group; see ambiguous. Roman aur and Urdu اور are refused.

homographs.why: also English 'char'; and 'char sau bees' (420) is the everyday idiom for a cheat, still read as 420 in a single amount field and in free text.
also the article 'a'; before a multiplier both readings are one.
also hyperbole ('lakh koshish'); findAmounts should not read a bare multiplier without a currency marker or a number beside it.
also the month Safar, written beside a day ('10 صفر'): two numbers with no multiplier, already refused; findAmounts (work item 5) should not read a date as an amount.
also the verb 'sleep' ('سو گیا') and a literary 'so'.
also 'new' in phrases such as 'سالِ نو'.
also a Persian word for 'why', rare in everyday Urdu.
